title.narrative: Sustainable and gender sensitive integration of IDPs in Pemba, Northern Mozambique, through the implementation of Urban Durable Solutions (Phase 2 – SDC funds)

description.narrative:
In 2022, the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN Habitat) and the International Organization for Migration (IOM) developed the joint program ‘Sustainable and gender sensitive integration of internally displaced persons (IDPs) in the Greater Pemba area through the implementation of Urban Durable Solutions’. This three-year programme (2022-2025) for a total of USD 9 million seeks to address the needs of IDPs and host communities in urban and peri-urban areas in and around Pemba, Cabo Delgado. This has been developed through the valuable contribution of many of the UN-Habitat branches and units and approved at Concept Note Stage in January 2022.
It has been then developed as a full ProDoc and approved by the PRC in March 2022, when a first implementation Phase with around 18% of the total program needs ($2M) has been funded by the High Commission for Canada in Mozambique, to kickstart the activities in a first pilot neighborhood in Pemba (Mahate). UN-Habitat signed a 2 years contract with the donor and through a UN to UN agreement engaged IOM, with whom the program was jointly developed. While the achievements under the joint program have shown a positive impact and great potential to be adapted and replicated in other neighborhoods and sites in the greater Pemba area, the program remains underfunded. A joint effort of the two agencies, to mainstream the approach and share it with key stakeholders, resulted in manifestations of interests from various partners who visited the activities in Mahate, such the Embassies of Japan, Belgium, Sweden and Switzerland among other. So far, the Phase 1 of the program funded by the High Commission of Canada has successfully achieved: • An Urban Profiling framework for Pemba was developed resulting in spatial understanding on how the city is responding to the rapid growth of population as well preliminary recommendations for emergency planning in urban areas, developing plans scenarios for short-, medium- and long-term sustainable integration of IDPs in Pemba. • A successful workshop was organized in December 2022, chaired by Municipality of Pemba with more than 50 participants among technician and representatives from different humanitarian and development partners working in Pemba and from government at different level including communities’ leaders and members from Mahate neighborhood. • An Active Public Space Observation walk was done in Mahate neighborhood to analyze the modalities of coexistence between the host community and the displaced, particularly women and girls. 52 potential areas of interventions were mapped and discussed with communities, namely People and Usage, Accessibility, Water and Sanitation Access, Comfort and Safety, and Environment. • Based on this a Neighborhood Gender Sensitive Action Plan has been elaborated with contributions of displaced and hosting communities, local authorities and civil society (on five strategic priority areas), and defining the public services and infrastructure that will be improved by the project at neighborhood level. • The preliminary project for the extension and resilient rehabilitation of the area of the neighborhood secretary in Mahate has been designed, considering inputs of the local leadership, the community and the MHPSS team, to work also a resource center for displaced and host community. • The community infrastructure portfolio has been designed and shared with relevant stakeholders for validation and it’s including:  WASH: Rehabilitation of 3 wells, construction of one small water distribution system with 4 water points and one public laundry point;  URBAN EQUIPMENT: Installation of 34 solar public illumination point in strategic roads and public spaces, improvement in signalization of road crossing, construction of 2 improved bus stops, improvement in equipment for waste collection;  NATURE-BASED SOLUTIONS: Improvement of one secondary road with drainage and erosion control, construction of one public space for youth and children • The project implemented activities to strengthen family and community support and provided focused MHPSS services in the neighborhood for the host and displaced communities. • 1,276 (710 female and 566 male) people participated in arts and sports events with socio-relational activities that aimed to reduce risk of isolation and marginalization while strengthening the community ties for improved social cohesion. • 1,974 people received focused MHPSS services to help cope with daily stressors as well as traumatic events connected to limited access to services, violence, and the effects of displacement. • 162 (113 women, 49 men) technicians from Government, displaced and host members from communities were trained on participatory planning using a gender-sensitive urban planning tool named “Her City” including gender-sensitive issues.
